rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a SiC coating applied by CVD, whereas the target uses a DC magnetron-sputtered AlTiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy coating with varied Al content. These are fundamentally different material systems and deposition methods.
rationale.condition_agreement: Both involve high-temperature steam oxidation at ~1000°C, but the target specifies flowing steam from ultrapure water at 0.2 mL/min, isothermal hold times of 60 min (and 30 min at 1100°C), and post-oxidation indentation, while the hypothesis proposes a 2-hour exposure without these specifics.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a generic physical barrier mechanism, whereas the target describes a specific mechanism involving preferential nucleation of Al2O3, TiO2, and Cr2O3 to form a composite oxide layer, with excess Al causing detrimental intermetallic formation and oxide discontinuity.
rationale.outcome_agreement: Both predict reduced oxidation rate and maintained integrity relative to an uncoated baseline, but the target specifies a non-monotonic Al-content dependence with an optimum at ~10 at.% and quantifies parabolic rate constants, while the hypothesis predicts a simple reduction for SiC.
